thread:
sam-marketing: Hey team — last-minute ask for tomorrow's demo. Can runtime run a very small, fast 'hourglass' warmup probe so we can validate coldstart/warmup behavior for the keynote demo? Need artifacts by 0900 PT.

Requirements: short run (<=30m), n=40 requests across 3 payload sizes (short/medium/long), both fp16 and 4-bit quantized variants, include per-request trace IDs, per-token latency histogram, and a coldstart heatmap. Also want one representative request payload + model logits snapshot for the long case.

Priority: high (we'll route a few demo leads if green).

jenna-runtime: Got it. We can do a quick probe. Two clarifying Qs: 1) which model(s) to run? 2) do you need KV-prefix caching enabled or explicitly disabled for this probe (we can test both but that'll double runs).

sam-marketing: Thanks — please run base-open-8b and opt-8b-q4 as the quantized variant. For caching: run without prefix caching (we want pure coldstart heatmap) + a single quick capped run with caching enabled for comparison (so two small runs total).

lee-platform: FYI GPU pool availability looks tight between 01:00-04:00 PT; recommend scheduling the runs at 05:30 PT to guarantee dedicated nodes. If team needs <30m we can still squeeze an earlier slot but no promises.

jenna-runtime: Scheduling 05:30 PT (1756668600) for coldstart-only runs, 06:10 PT for cached comparison. We'll limit to 40 requests each and cap concurrency to 4 to mimic demo env. Will produce: consolidated CSV of per-request latencies, histograms (p50/p90/p99), heatmap PNG, and a tarball with traces + one logits snapshot.

maya.ops: I'll queue the jobs and attach the run IDs here. Also will add a short runbook note so people know how to interpret the heatmap (cold rows = no warmup; brighter rows = longer first-token latency).

sam-marketing: Awesome. Do we have a minimal curl command or CLI the team can use to re-run locally if needed? Prefer something we can paste into the rehearsal docs.

jenna-runtime: Yep — here's the lightweight runner we use for quick probes: ```bash
ri-bench run \ 
  --model base-open-8b \ 
  --variant fp16 \ 
  --cohort-size 40 \ 
  --concurrency 4 \ 
  --payloads ./hourglass_payloads/{short,medium,long}.json \ 
  --record-traces \ 
  --out ./out/hourglass_fp16_run.tar.gz
```
For the quantized run: change --model to opt-8b-q4 and --variant q4. To disable caching: add --kv-cache disabled.

runtime-bot: Job queued: run_id=rb-1756666701 (coldstart_fp16), estimated 18m.

jenna-runtime: Started coldstart_fp16 (rb-1756666701). Monitoring logs.

maya.ops: run_id=rb-1756666701 completed. Artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/runs/rb-1756666701/hourglass_fp16.tar.gz. CSV and heatmap inside.

sam-marketing: ✅ Received. Quick glance: long payload p99 looks a bit spiky — can you attach the representative logits snapshot and the trace for that specific request ID (trace: trace-8472)?

jenna-runtime: Attached in the tarball: traces/trace-8472.json and snapshots/logits-8472.npy.gz. Putting a short note: the p99 spike was during first token decode on node gpu-dedicated-3 when a background GC hit the allocator; not related to model runtime itself.

lee-platform: Noted — we'll spin a short test on gpu-dedicated-4 to verify allocation jitter isn't systemic. If we see repeatable spikes we'll escalate.

sam-marketing: Perfect. Last ask: can you add a one-paragraph summary that marketing can paste into rehearsal notes (3–4 bullets: what we tested, key artifacts, any risk flags)?

jenna-runtime: Posted summary: "Hourglass warmup probe (n=40, short/medium/long) for base-open-8b (fp16) and opt-8b-q4 (q4). Produced per-request latencies, heatmap, traces, and a logits snapshot for long payloads. Observed isolated p99 spike tied to allocator GC on gpu-dedicated-3; not reproducible on gpu-dedicated-4. Action: monitor overnight; recommend using the 05:30 PT slot for demo to avoid noisy window."

sam-marketing: Exactly what we needed — thanks y'all :party_parrot: Closing this thread, will ping if rehearsal needs another rerun.
